newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says many foreign miners keen on Yauliyacu.
newsitem.headline: Peru says many foreign miners keen on Yauliyacu.

text.p: Peru's state mining company Centromin said Monday at least eight local and "many" foreign miners were interested in the November 15 auction of its polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yauliyacu S.A.
"Many consortia from all around the world have come and shown their interest," said Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares.
He added some of the foreign companies interested were from Canada and the United States and that some of the local miners were forming consortia with foreigners ahead of the auction.
Centromin will receive offers on November 11 from companies interested in bidding at the auction.
Yauliyaca, based in the province of Huarochiri, 75 miles (120 km) east of Lima, includes an underground mine and a concentrating plant with capacity to treat 980,000 tonnes of mineral per year.
Centromin said the unit has proven and probable reserves of silver, zinc, lead and copper totalling 7.3 million tonnes. The unit's potential reserves total 14.7 million tonnes.
In 1995, 746,000 tonnes of mineral were extracted from the site.
In July, Centromin launched its piecemeal sell-off with the successful auction of two of the company's major assets - the copper-rich Antamina prospect and the Quicay gold prospect.
However, last month, the government declared void its intended auction of state-run polymetallic mine Yauricocha because of a lack of bids.
-- Saul Hudson, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134 REUTER SH AC
